title: SYSK’s Fall True Crime Playlist: The Hinterkaifeck Axe Murders
summary: Fall true crime playlist opener from Stuff You Should Know, covering the unsolved 1922 Hinterkaifeck farm murders in the village of Kaifeck, Bavaria, where the Gruber family, a maid, and a two-year-old were bludgeoned with a mattock. The hosts walk through the weird pre-murder events (footprints in snow, missing keys, scratched lock, a strange newspaper), the discovery of the bodies, suspects Lorenz Schlittenbauer and Carl Gabriel, the botched skull analysis, and a 2007 Munich police academy investigation. The episode closes with a listener mail about a squirrel hunt and a plug for a candle company. Note: the host's name is Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant; a pronunciation segment covers the German names.

segments.title: Playlist introduction
segments.summary: Josh introduces the fall true crime playlist and lists other true crime episodes that were not included.

segments.title: Opening banter and Halloween tie-in
segments.summary: Hosts say this is a creepy bonus episode near Halloween and warn listeners about the subject matter.

segments.title: German pronunciation and the Gruber family
segments.summary: The hosts work through pronunciations of Hinterkaifeck, Kaifeck, and family names, then introduce the Gruber family of the farm: Andreas, Cäzilia, daughter Victoria, granddaughter, and two-year-old Joseph.

segments.title: Family background and reputation
segments.summary: The Grubers were wealthy but disliked. Andreas was reportedly abusive and controlling, and rumors claimed Joseph was born of incest; the hosts doubt the rumor.

segments.title: Maid quits and footprints in the snow
segments.summary: A maid quits, saying the house is haunted. Later Andreas finds a single set of footprints leading to the house in snow with none leading away.

segments.title: Strange events in March 1922
segments.summary: Andreas searches the property and finds scratches on a tool shed lock. Keys go missing, a strange newspaper appears on the porch, and Andreas hears footfalls inside the house.

segments.title: Discovery of the bodies
segments.summary: A new maid, Maria Baumgartner, starts March 31, 1922. On April 4 neighbors notice the family missing from church and school and go check. They find the Pomeranian tied in the barn and the bodies of Andreas, Victoria, and Cäzilia in the barn, plus Joseph and the maid in the house, all bludgeoned.

segments.title: Autopsy, mattock, and timeline
segments.summary: Doctor Johann R. Mueller performs autopsies and concludes a mattock was the weapon. Cäzilia was found with hair in her fists, suggesting she survived for hours. Neighbors saw smoke and signs of care, suggesting the killer stayed for days.

segments.title: Lorenz Schlittenbauer as suspect
segments.summary: Neighbor Lorenz Schlittenbauer, reputed father of Joseph, had a paternity dispute and faced a possible suit. He was in the search party, disturbed the crime scene, knew the house layout, and claimed to have spent the night in a barn with no strong alibi. He lived about 350 meters away.

segments.title: Carl Gabriel and other theories
segments.summary: Carl Gabriel, Victoria's former husband believed dead in World War One, was proposed as a suspect; WWII reports and police checks are discussed. Ghost and paranormal theories are dismissed.

segments.title: Skulls, suspects, and investigation loss
segments.summary: Police decapitated the victims and sent skulls for analysis; a clairvoyant was consulted; the skulls went missing, possibly in WWII Nuremberg. Over one hundred suspects were interviewed. The hosts find Schlittenbauer the most likely culprit but say no hard evidence exists.

segments.title: 2007 police academy investigation and tangents
segments.summary: Students of a Munich police academy investigated in 2007 and concluded the living suspect was probably responsible, without naming him. The hosts digress into Steve Guttenberg and Party Down.

segments.title: Wrap-up of Hinterkaifeck resources
segments.summary: Hosts mention other sources on Hinterkaifeck, including Stuff You Missed in History Class and Mysterious Universe.

segments.title: Thanks to donors
segments.summary: Hosts thank Margaret and Mike of Jacksonville, Florida for helping with the show's army.

segments.title: Listener mail: squirrel shooting
segments.summary: A listener recounts shooting a squirrel with a pellet gun at age thirteen, not killing it cleanly, and deciding never to hunt for sport again. He also plugs his dog-themed candle company.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts give social media and website information and sign off.

segments.title: Closing credits
segments.summary: Closing line directing listeners to HowStuffWorks.
